NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard which is identical with IEC 1020-3/IEC QC 960500 (1991) `Electromechanical switches for use in electronic equipment - Part 3 : Sectional specification for in-line package switches' issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendation of Electromechanical Components and Mechanical Structures for Electronic Equipment Sectional Committee (LTD 7) and approval of the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. The text of the IEC standard has been approved as suitable for publication as Indian Standard without deviations. Certain conventionsare, however, not identical to those used in Indian Standards. Attention is particularly drawn to the following: a) b) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear referring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. Comma (,) has been used as a decimal marker while in indian Standards, the correct practice is to use a point (.) as the decimal marker.

Only the English language text in the International Standard has been retained while adopting it in this Indian Standard. This standard is intended primarily for use under IECQ system. ELECTROMECHANICAL SWITCHES FOR USE IN ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT
PART 3 SECTIONAL SPECIFICATION FOR IN-LINE PACKAGE SWITCHES 1 1.1 General Scope

This part of IEC 1020 applies to the sub-family of in-line package switches within the family of electromechanical switches of assessed quality. In-line package switches covered by this part of IEC 1020 are designed for use with printed boards as an interface with analog and digital logic circuits.

This part of IEC 1020 includes, of in-line package switches: _ -

but `is not necessarily

limited to, the following

sub-families

rotary actuated DIP (duai-in-line slide actuated DIP switches; rocker actuated DIP switches; toggle actuated DIP switches.

b) select the IEC 1020-l ;

1.3

Terminoiogy in IEC 1020-1, the following definition shall apply

In addition to the terminology specified to all in-line package switches.

1.3.1 In-line package switch: A manually operated, multiple section electromechanical switch with one or more movable actuators and with terminations arranged in parallel rows on a specified grid. 1.4 Marking

The marking requirements of IEC 1020-l apply; in addition, the marking shall include the identification of the switch poles. Moreover, when specified by the relevant specification, the "on" and/or "off" positions of the switch actuator shall be marked on the switch. 1.5 Detail specification shall be derived from the relevant blank detail specification. requirements which

Detail specifications

Detail specifications shall not specify test severities or performance are less than those specified in this part of IEC 1020.

When more severe test severities or performance requirements are included, they shall be clearly described in the detail specification and shall be indicated in the test schedules by a special notation such as an asterisk. If the technical requirements of the generic and/or sectional specification relative to inspection are not entirely suitable (either for technical reasons or because of special applications) to the in-line package switch described in the detail specification, the detail specification shall set out clearly the modifications which are to be made to these requirements. The detail specification shall state, directly or by reference to other standards, all information necessary to completely describe all interchangeability parameters for that type of in-line package switch, including any styles and variants, and to ensure conformance thereof with all requirements for quality assurance.

The following information prescribed shall preferably part of IEC 1020.

shall be given in each detail specification and the values be selected from those given in the applicable clause of this

1.51

Preparation of detail specifications

The detail specification shall contain all the necessary information to identify the particular type, style(s) and variant(s) of in-line package switches which it covers. This information shall include at least the following, if applicable:

c) d)

1.52

ratings and characteristics; outline and detailed dimensions; number of poles; functional operation; sealed or non-sealed; mechanical operating characteristics; terminations; contact arrangement; mounting details; assessment level. Outline and detailed dimensions

There shall be an illustrat.ion or a drawing of the in-line package switch as an aid to easy recognition and for comparison with other types of in-line package switches. Drawings shall be either first angle or third angle projection. The projection method shall be stated by the detail specification. Illustrations shall be an isometric view.

The dimensional limits necessary for mounting and interchangeability shall be prescribed in the drawing with variable dimensions given in a table. All dimensions shall be stated in millimetres. Where the original dimensions are in inches, the inch dimensions shall be given in brackets. 1.5.3 Moutijng dimensions

The in-line package switch shall be mounted by the termination on a 254 mm x 254 mm (0,100 in x 0,100 in) grid system for printed boards. 1.5.4 Safety requirements

lf necessary, safety requirements shall be specified in the detail specification by reference to the relevant safety specification. 2 2.1 Preferred ratings and characterlstlcs

Rated voltages

The preferred d.c. voltage ratings are 6 V, 24 V and 50 V. 2.2 Rated currents

The following current ratings are preferred: 10 mA, 100 mA and 250 mA.

Quality assessment Qualification

procedures

approval procedures

Qualification approval procedures shall be as prescribed by 3.4 of IEC 1020-l and the following. a) The tests required for qualification approval used for approval of a single style of switch. are prescribed in table 1 and shall be

For approval of multiple styles of the same switch type, the total quantity of test specimens for each test and the proportion of each representative style shall be proposed by the manufacturer and shall be, accepted by the National Supervising Inspectorate. Spare test specimens are permitted. The principles of structural similarity may be applied. After completion of group 0 tests, the sample shall be divided for the other groups. The tests within a group shall be performed in the order shown except that group 0 tests may be performed in any sequence. Specimens groups. found defective during the tests of group 0 shall not be used for other

"One defective" is counted ments of a group.

when a switch has not satisfied

all or part of the require-

Qualification approval is granted when the number of defectives does not exceed the specified number of permissible defectives for each group and the total number of permissible defectives for each group. The conditions of test and the performance requirements shall be the same as for quality conformance inspection. for,qualification approval tests

b) Test specimens shall be as specified in the detail representative of the range of products described in it.

specification

and shall

be

c) The number of contact sets tested may be reduced for multipole, multiposition inline package switches if the manufacturer considers that the complexity of the switches renders this desirable. The reduction of test specimens shall be according to the following rules: if the specified sample size is "n" switches, then the test samples shall consist of *n" complete switches; - a minimum proportion of these switches, as specified shall have all their mechanisms and contacts tested; by the detail specification,

- the remaining switches shall have all their mechanisms tested, but the quantity of their contact sets to be tested may be reduced to not less than a minimum, as specified by the detail specification, provided that: i) contacts shall be tested as complete sets, and

ii) contact sets to be tested shall be selected prior to the start of the series of tests and shali not then be re-selected; they shall be chosen at random from all samples and (where construction is modular) from all modules, ensuring that the selection is fully representative of the distribution of contact set types in the sample, and iii) at least one contact set shall be tested from each switch, and iv) the same contacts shall be used for all tests.

3.2

Quality conformance

inspection and the

Quality conformance inspection shall be as prescribed by 3.5 of IEC 1020-l following requirements.

a) The lot-by-lot inspection tests are prescribed in the blank detail specification. The sequence of tests is optional unless otherwise specified. Inspection level II or S2 shall apply.. b) The periodic inspection tests are prescribed in the blank detail specification.

An inspection lot may consist of structurally similar switches provided the conditions of 3.3 of IEC 1020-l are met. For periodic inspections, the proportion of test specimens of different styles shall be the same as for qualification approval tests. Ail test specimens which are subjected to periodic inspections shall have passed group A tests. The conditions of test and the, performance requirements for the quality conformance inspection shall be the same as for the qualification approval. The prescribed AQL's apply to each attribute inspected during the test. At the manufacturer's option, a more stringent AQL may be used.

a

IS QC 960500

: 1999 IEC CC 960500 : 1991

3.3

Delayed deliveries

Switches held for more than three years following the release of the inspection lot shall be re-examined in accordance with the specified lot-by-lot inspection tests prior to delivery. The procedure for the re-examination shall be approved by the National Supervising Inspectorate. Once a lot has been re-examined, its quality is reassured for three more years. Switches with solderable terminals which are held more than one year following the release of the inspection lot shall be re-examined for solderability prior to delivery. The procedure for the re-examination shall be approved by the National Supervising inspectorate. Once a lot has been re-examined for solderability, its quality is assured for one more year. 4 Test methods and requirements

This clause supplements the test methods and requirements of IEC 1020-l. 4.1 Vibration shall be supplemented as follows.

The method of the vibration test (4.7.2 of IEC 1020-l)

a) The frequency range shall be 10 Hz to 55 Hz, 10 Hz to 150 Hz, 10 Hz to 500 Hz or 10 Hz to 2 000 Hz as specified by the detail specification. b) For the frequency range of 10 Hz to 55 Hz, the displacement amplitude shall be 0.75 mm. For other frequency ranges, the acceleration amplitude shall be 147 m/s* (15 g) peak or 98 m/s* (10 g) peak as specified by the detail specification. 4.2 Electrical endurance - standard atmospheric conditions

The method of the electrical endurance - atmospheric conditions test (4.10.1 of IEC 1020-l) shall be supplemented as follows. If more than one electrical rating is specified, the electrical test loads may be evenly distributed among the test specimens. 4.3 Climatic sequence shall be supplemented as

The method of the climatic sequence test (4.12.1 of IEC 1020-l) foliows.

The number of cycles to be performed during the cyclic damp heat test shall be determined by the duration specified for the damp heat, steady state test (4.12.2 of IEC 1020-l) as follows: Damp heat, steady state 4 10 21 56 days days days days Damp heat, cyclic 1 1 2 6 cycle with assisted recovery cycle cycles cycles

4.4

Machine soldering
- This test is provisional pending confirmation of the uniformity and NOTE results. Further consideration is being given to the details of the test method. reproducibility of the test

Object: The objective of the test is the assessment of the ability of the switch to withstand the environmental effects of automated machine soldering and the associated fluxing, preheating, soldering and cleaning operations. Equipment: A conventional wave soldering machine with provisions for fluxing and preheating shall be used. The wave soldering machine shall be capable of producing the specified test conditions. Alternative equipment: As an alternative, the following equipment may be used: a controlled foam fluxing operation system capable of producing the fluxing action required; a suitable means to increase the temperature of the printed board assembly to the specified value; a solder pot of sufficient size to allow the dipping of the prfnted board assembly and to contain a sufficient volume of solder to ensure a uniform temperature of the solder during immersion of the printed board assembly; _ suitable containers for the cleaning solution and the means to create the specified vapour and/or spray. ~aferfals: The materials used for the test shall be as follows: _

a) The solder and the flux shall be as specified in IEC 68-2-20. Activated flux may be used when specified by the detail specification. The flux may be coioured to aid in detection. b) The material for the printed board shall be epoxy glass or equivalent with 35 urn thick copper. The mounting holes shall be of the minimum diameter specified by the detail specification. The copper pad shall completely surround and abut the mounting hole. The minimum width of the annular ring around the mounting hole shall be 0.13 mm (0,005 in) far plated-through holes and 0,38 mm (0,015 in) for other holes.
Method:

The test shall be performed in accordance with the following details.

a) The switch shall be fully inserted into the printed board. Unless otherwise specified, the switch shall not be cleaned; however, care shall be taken to prevent contamination of the terminals by oil, grease, perspiration, etc. The printed board shall be cleaned to assure solderability. Multiple test specimens and different switch styles may be mounted on a single printed board. b) The printed board assembly shall be fluxed in such a manner that the foam of flux will comply with one of the following conditions as specified by the detail specification. i) Condition A: Foam shall contact both the bottom surface of the printed board and the bottom surface of the switch body within the immediate area of the terminals. ii) Condition B: Foam shall contact both the bottom surface of the printed board but not contact the switch body.

: 1999 IEC QC 960500 : 1991 IS QC 960500

c) The printed board assembly shall be subjected to an evenly distributed preheating of 78 "C to 93 OC for a period of 30 s to 60 s immediately prior to soldering. The preheat temperature shall be measured on the top surface (component side ) of the printed board. d) The solder temperature shall be 260 "C f 5 "C for the soldering operation. The duration of the immersion of each terminal in the solder shall be 2, 4, 6, 8 or 10 s as specified by the detail specification. e) After soldering, all visible flux shall be removed by.applying a cleaning solvent by a vapour and spray, spray only or immersion as specified by the detail specification. The cleaning solution shall be in accordance with the following as specified by the detail specification. i) ii) l-l - 1 trichloroethane; l-1-2 trichlorotrifluoroethane (isopropyl alcohol); (45 % butyl according to IEC 68-2-45;

iii) P-propanol

iv) a mixture of de-ionized water 90 % by volume and alkaline detergent cellosolve, 45 % monoethanolamine, 10 % water) 10 % by volume. v) none (washing of the switch not permitted).

f) The markings shall be examined in accordance with the visual examination (4.3.1 of IEC 1020-l). The switch shall be subjected to the functional operation (4.3.5 of IEC 1020-l), the contact resistance test (4.4.2.1 or 4.4.2.2 of IEC 1020-l) the insulation resistance test (4.4.3 of IEC 1020-l). g) The internal surfaces of the switch shall be examined 20x magnification with illumination. for the presence

test test and

of flux under

~equkementsr

After the test, the markings shall be legible and there shall be no damage which impairs the electrical or mechanical operation of the switch. There shall be no flux on the internal surfaces of the switch.
